description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's West Africa Regional Programme works to deepen trade integration and reduce the cost of cross-border commerce across ECOWAS and AfCFTA member states, operating since 2023 through strategic partnerships with the AfCFTA Secretariat, ECOWAS Commission, and UEMOA to address the regulatory fragmentation, corridor inefficiencies, and non-tariff barriers that continue to constrain intra-regional trade despite significant tariff liberalisation. The Programme operates across three mutually reinforcing levels i.e regional policy harmonisation, corridor-level facilitation, and country-specific competitiveness, advancing customs cooperation and digitisation, strengthening integrated and coordinated border management, and upgrading SPS and standards frameworks to support compliance-based trade across member states.

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Revenue collected attributable to digital infrastructure projects supported by integration of the ECOWAS’ SIGMAT system with the Ghanaian ICUMS customs.

comment.narrative: 47% increase in customs receipts at Akanu-Noepe, Ghana. 40% increase in customs revenues from $22 million in 2024 to $28 million between January and October 2025 with a projection of 67% increase year on year after improvements in real-time customs data transmission following TMA-supported integration of the ECOWAS’ SIGMAT system with the Ghanaian ICUMS customs system.

title.narrative: Estimated reduction in GHG emissions (in CO₂ equivalent) resulting from enhanced green infrastructure interventions.

comment.narrative: 90 -100 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions avoided and 280–320 MWh of renewable energy annually, delivering resilient, low carbon power and safer, more efficient operations at Akanu–Noepe JBP, with the completion of the phased renewable energy upgrade at Akanu–Noepe JBP, strengthening border operational resilience and improving safety, security and efficiency.
